questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 100 mL of 1.0 M aqueous NaOH solution was diluted to 1.0 L by adding water. Half of this solution was discarded. A new 100 mL of 0.5 M aqueous NaOH solution was added to the remaining solution. What is the concentration of the final aqueous NaOH solution?
questions.solution:
Initial millimoles of NaOH = $100 \times 1.0 = 100$ mmol.

Volume after dilution = $1.0$ L = $1000$ mL.

Molarity after dilution = $\dfrac{100}{1000} = 0.1$ M.

Half of the solution is discarded, so the remaining volume is $500$ mL.

Millimoles of NaOH in the remaining solution = $500 \times 0.1 = 50$ mmol.

Millimoles of NaOH added = $100 \times 0.5 = 50$ mmol.

Total millimoles of NaOH in the final solution = $50 + 50 = 100$ mmol.

Total volume of the final solution = $500 + 100 = 600$ mL.

Final concentration = $\dfrac{100}{600} = \dfrac{1}{6} \approx 0.1667$ M $\approx 0.17$ M.

Answer: $0.17$ M
